newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. Dec durable goods drop 1.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. Dec durable goods drop 1.7 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Commerce Department reported durable goods orders fell 1.7 percent in December versus a revised decline of 1.7 percent in November.
U.S. economists in a Reuters survey had expected a 1.2-percent rise in December durable goods orders.

DAVID BLITZER, CHIEF ECONOMIST, STANDARD & POOR'S: "Some people will begin to rethink the most buoyant (Gross Domestic Product) figures ... This is always a very volatile report; it's always difficult to mesh in (with other data)."
Blitzer was speaking on Reuters Financial Television.

PETER KRETZMER, SENIOR ECONOMIST, NATIONSBANC CAPITAL MARKETS INC: "This is a very volatile series, but I don't see much of a reaction -- maybe a quarter point gain (in the U.S. Treasury bond) at most.
"The defense sector was missed by econmomists, but it still may show business investment slowed some in the fourth quarter," Kretzmer added.

MICHAEL NIEMIRA, ECONOMIST, BANK OF TOKYO-MITSUBISHI LTD: "It's surprisingly weak. The question is how much of this is temporary and we get a bounceback because these numbers are extremely volatile. But certainly the December report is soft, clearly the reason for the turnaround in the bond market.

"There are some signs within the report that suggest it's not as weak as it appears on the surface -- such as primary metals up 2.2 percent, industrial machinery up 1.5 percent. It's not so uniform and the big part of this story is the electronic component category dropped 12.5 percent," he added.

WILLIAM GRIGGS, MANAGING DIRECTOR, GRIGGS & SANTOW INC: "The fact that the softness was broad-based means these numbers should be good for the bond market. The widespread feeling was we would see an up number.

"It seems the story with orders right along has been supportive of a moderate growth economy. This report doesn't change the very moderate uptrend in orders and in fact underscores the softness in the economy," he added.
